Task: run an impeccable-style design pass on the conversation reader and the reply/compose surfaces of Email OS (Vue 3 desktop email client), then implement the fixes.

Context: a UI/UX review of the whole app ranked this area as the next one to focus on (22/40 heuristics, attention 8/10). The review was done from code only (nothing was rendered), so treat findings as strong leads and verify them. Read PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md first (brand: focused, precise, trustworthy; keyboard-first; honest state; message content renders as safe literal plain text; drafts are local-only; no Send exists by design). Look at .impeccable/critique/*.md for the format and tone of prior critiques (inbox list and search were already done; don't redo them). superhuman-email-browsing-ux-spec.md and docs/ux-02-conversation-reader.md describe the reference. Don't import Superhuman scope beyond browsing/reading/reply look and feel.

Files in scope: src/components/ReaderView.vue, ComposeCard.vue, ReplyComposer.vue, DraftEditorCore.vue, AttachmentChooser.vue, the reader/compose mounting in src/App.vue (~lines 2400-2620), src/lib/browsing-actions.ts / action-palette.ts for shortcuts, src/assets/style.css, and tests (reader*, compose-card, reply-composer, attachments).

Findings to verify and address, in priority order:
1. P1 No reply shortcut. There is no `r` key; the only entry to prepareReply (App.vue:1587) is the reader's icon (ReaderView ~709-720, ~848). Add R (and show the shortcut hint in the palette/reader), respecting editable/IME shortcut protection.
2. P1 Reply composer is a form: four always-visible labelled fields (To, Cc, Subject, Body) in a 2-column grid (DraftEditorCore ~100-113). Make it a compact docked reply: collapsed "To: name" recipient row, Cc and Subject on demand, body focused on open. Quoted source block (ReplyComposer ~156-166) is monospace 0.85rem and clashes with the reading face; use the UI/reading font with secondary colour.
3. P1 Permanent 3-line disclaimer in the composer (DraftEditorCore ~93-96) and raw IDs in "Reply source is fixed: <conversationId> · <messageId>" (ReplyComposer ~105). Replace with one honest line, e.g. "Saved locally · not sent"; move detail into a title/popover; never show raw IDs. Footer should have a clear primary action and visible shortcut hints.
4. P1 Reader header carries up to six stacked caveat paragraphs (ReaderView ~778-816), including "Opening this conversation does not change read state" on every open. Collapse standing caveats to one muted status line; surface only exceptions (blocked reply, incomplete, snapshot) inline; keep the honesty, drop the repetition.
5. P2 Quoted `>` blocks and signatures are not collapsed and force the whole body into monospace (message-body-format.ts, bodyNeedsMonospace). Collapse trailing quoted lines behind a "Show quoted text" disclosure (still plain text, no HTML rendering) so prose stays proportional.
6. P2 Attachments are second-class: no per-message attachment rows in the thread, only the Cmd+O chooser; AttachmentChooser shows raw "N bytes" and a wall of copy. Add inline attachment rows (name, human size, Save) and tidy the chooser.
7. P2 Loading state is a bare "Loading conversation..." (ReaderView ~742); P3 collapsed-message sender column and uppercased date differ from the list's type system (style.css ~1507, ~1526); reply composer max-height 45% / 5rem textarea leaves ~3 visible lines.
Also keep contrast in mind: Graphite (#8e8a87) is under 3:1 on the focus fill; don't use it for meaningful glyphs on focused surfaces.

Constraints: honour every "Standing constraints" and Anti-references item in PRODUCT.md (no AI magic, no optimistic UI that lies, no card stacks). Do not regress existing behaviour: explicit action labels, editable/IME shortcut protection, reduced-motion, announcements, focus handling, J/K reader navigation smoothness. Keep copy terse, sentence-case, factual. Do NOT touch the empty-inbox/account/first-run state (App.vue ~2473) or other areas; that is a separate piece of work. No real provider writes.

Process: first write a short critique of the area to .impeccable/critique/ in the existing format (verify the findings above by reading the code and tests; note any that turn out to be wrong). Then use the repo's `implement` skill / persona-feature-engineer agent to implement, update or add tests, run the project's checks (see mise.toml and docs/development.md; run pnpm install first if node_modules is missing), and update DESIGN.md if tokens or patterns change. Commit on this branch and open a PR to main. Report back with what changed, what you verified, what you could not verify (e.g. no rendered screenshots), and any findings you rejected.
I'll start by reading the product docs and prior critiques.

163	# Design System: Email OS
164	
165	## 1. Overview
166	
167	**Creative North Star: "The Quiet Instrument"**
168	
169	A precision tool used in long, focused sessions. The surface is a single warm charcoal plane. The interface recedes until only the list, the open conversation and the next decision are on screen. Density is high but calm: 36px rows, small type, no dividers, no cards. One violet signal marks where you are. Everything else is a tonal step on the same warm gray ramp.
170	
171	The system follows Superhuman's browsing look closely, and that parity is an explicit goal. It covers geometry, density, type scale, tonal layering and the focused-row treatment. Features and workflows stay our own. The one place we deliberately go our own way is state: pending, failed, partial and outcome-unknown states are always visible in their own form (*"Honest state over smooth feel"*, PRODUCT.md). A quiet surface must never hide what happened.
172	
173	The system rejects Gmail-web clutter, "AI magic" sparkle chrome, generic SaaS dashboards (card grids, gradient heroes, oversized rounded panels), and optimistic UI that says "Done" before the provider confirms.
174	
175	**Key Characteristics:**
176	- Three fixed panes: a 40px icon rail, a fluid list or reader, and a 272px darker contact pane. Each is separated by a single 1px divider.
177	- One content inset (50px from the list pane's left edge). It aligns split tabs, sender names, date-group captions, notices, banners and the bottom dock.
178	- 36px rows on 12px type. Hierarchy comes from weight and tone, not size.
179	- Pane-edge alignment: the contact name sits on the split-tab line, and the contact email sits on the first-row line.
180	- Flat tonal layering. No shadows in the browsing shell.
181	- The violet accent appears once per screen: on the focused row or the active message.
182	
183	**Layout geometry (approximate calibration targets).** These values come from the 2026-11-07 Superhuman reference capture (1603×2000 image px). The capture was scaled by about 1.56 image px per CSS px, calibrated from the macOS traffic-light pitch of 20pt and cross-checked against the 36px rhythm and the 40px and 270px pane widths in `superhuman-email-browsing-ux-spec.md`. Verify them on real displays.
184	- **Rail:** 40px wide. The top action button (28px circle) is centered on the split-tab line (42px down). The navigation icons sit in a dark pill about 30px wide that starts near the header's bottom edge, with its first glyph centered on the first list line (96px down) and a 28px pitch. The active glyph sits on a 24px Rail Pebble disc inside the pill.
185	- **Split header:** 78px from the content top to the first row. Tabs are vertically centered about 42px down. The hamburger is centered 23px into the pane. Tabs start at the 50px content inset with an 18px gap; the count sits 4px after its label. Compose and search icons are right-aligned on the 32px action pitch.
186	- **Rows:** 36px. The highlight is inset 6px from both pane edges. There is a 44px left gutter, with the 5px unread dot centered about 34px into the row. The sender column is 132px, and subject→snippet→meta gaps are 12px. The trailing date sits about 25px from the pane edge. On focus, three 16px action glyphs replace the date at a 32px pitch.
187	- **Date groups:** a 48px block, with the caption vertically centered on the content inset.
188	- **Contact pane:** 272px with a 24px inner inset. The name is centered on the tab line (42px), the email on the first list line (96px), the "Mail" label about 36px lower (~131px) and the first thread at ~156px, then a 24px pitch. Superhuman's footer toolbar sits 24px from the bottom: a ghost label plus 16px glyphs at a 28px pitch.
189	
190	### Parity Gaps (current code → target)
191	
192	This is the backlog for layout, typeset and polish passes. Each gap names what ships today and what this spec requires.
193	
194	1. **Split header.** Done (2026-11-07 header pass). The header is one borderless 78px strip inside the list column (the rail and contact pane span its height). It has a Graphite hamburger (Destinations navigator) centered 23px in, split tabs on the 50px inset (16px, active Paper White, inactive Smoke, 11px Ash count 4px after the label, 18px apart), and right-hand glyphs on the 32px pitch: Back (when there is history), Reminders (fixture only), the Starred-only toggle, Commands and Search. There is no brand text, no visible h1 while a tab is active, and no bordered chips. Glyphs are local inline SVG (`HeaderGlyph.vue`).
195	   - The context h1 stays in the accessibility tree. It is shown on screen, styled like an active tab, only when no rendered tab is active (Cached Done, Starred, Search, the reader, an open drawer).
196	   - The status line is removed. The inbox count is on the active tab; loaded counts were dropped as duplicates of the list. Selection count stays in SelectionBar, plus a visually hidden polite announcement. The pending count is covered by row "Pending…", the action notice and Activity. The Shift+U hint is in the Commands palette. The command error is its own alert line beside the action notice in the list column's bottom dock (gap 13). The read-only hint and the Unread-only/Starred-only filter states stay visible in words in the header.
197	   - The Inbox coverage sentence is the tabs' accessible description and the tab strip's hover title. The browser-preview banner is a one-line amber "Preview · in-memory" note on the right; the full disclosure is its title and accessible text.
198	   - Utility drawers now start below the header, so they never cover its glyphs.
199	   Update: the compose glyph now ships. It sits on the right of the header, left of Search, as a Graphite glyph on the 32px pitch, and opens the local-draft compose card INLINE in the central pane ("New Message", C key / palette action "Compose new local draft") — an in-flow card that replaces the list while composing, not a modal overlay: no backdrop and no dimming, so the rail, header and contact pane stay visible. (While a reader is open, the card docks at the bottom of the reader pane, like the reply composer.) There is still no compose capability beyond local drafts, so the glyph opens the local-only inline card, never a sender. (The aggregate pending count now lives on the Activity rail badge, and the tab line is calibrated against the rail's home circle: both are centered 42px down; see gap 2.)
200	2. **Rail.** Done (2026-11-07 rail/contact layout pass). The rail is a fixed 40px column (px, so larger root fonts widen the list, never the rail) with a 1px Seam on its right.
201	   - **Home circle:** Inbox is the 28px Rail Pebble circle, centered on the split-tab line. We have no AI or compose action to put there, so the primary destination takes the slot instead of an empty or dead control.
202	   - **Inkwell pill:** a 30px pill (the capture measures ~30px, not 28px) holds Starred (Gmail), Cached Done, Provider mail and Cached Trash (Gmail) as 16px glyphs on 28px hit targets at a 28px pitch. Its first glyph is centered on the first list line.
203	   - **Utilities:** Account (Gmail), Activity, Drafts and the narrow-viewport Contact disclosure are ghost glyphs at the bottom, 16px from the edge.
204	   - **States:** the current destination (`aria-current`) or open drawer (`aria-expanded`) shows a Paper White glyph on a 24px Rail Pebble disc; the rest are Graphite and rise to Paper White on hover and focus.
205	   - **Labels:** every button keeps its text label as its accessible name (a visually hidden span, so `textContent` is unchanged), its hover `title` (the action label with its shortcut, as on the header glyphs), and a keyboard tooltip: the same label shown beside the rail on `:focus-visible`, with Popover lift.
206	   - **Activity badge:** a small Amber Notice count on the Activity glyph shows unresolved operations, i.e. `queued`/`applying` plus `outcome_unknown`. It is derived from the activity rows the drawer already lists, with no new read. The digit is `aria-hidden`; the words ("2 operations pending", "1 operation with outcome unknown", or "3 operations unresolved: 2 pending, 1 outcome unknown") are the button's `aria-describedby` and are appended to its title. The badge disappears at zero.
207	   - **Glyphs:** local inline SVG in `PaneGlyph.vue` (Starred reuses HeaderGlyph's star). The rail sits at z-index 20 (above the row popover at 6, below drawers at 30).
208	   Remaining: the badge counts only what the activity snapshot carries (the same rows Activity shows), not a separate mailbox-wide total. The Contact disclosure stays in the rail below 1000px; it has no Superhuman analogue.
209	3. **Row metrics.** Done (2026-11-07 rows pass): 12px type in two weights, a fixed 36px height, no per-row dividers, the 6px pane inset, the 44px left gutter and the 132px sender column. Leading caption: done (polish pass). When the list opens with Today, that caption is visually hidden (it stays in the accessibility tree), so the first row is centered on the 96px first-list line with the rail's first glyph and the contact email, as in the reference. Today's rows already show a time, so nothing is lost on screen. Any other leading bucket (Yesterday, Earlier this month, a month, Unknown date) stays visible, because a list that starts in the past must say where it starts; in that case the first row is still centered 144px down.
210	4. **Focused row.** Done (rows pass): the fill is inset 6px from both pane edges, with a 4px Dusk Lavender bar on its own left edge.
211	5. **Read state.** Done (rows pass): a 5px `unread-marker` dot in the gutter, a distinct hollow ring when read state is unknown, and read senders drop to weight 400.
212	6. **Selection checkbox.** Done (rows pass): hidden until selection mode, hover or focus, and placed in the 44px gutter.
213	7. **Row actions.** Done (rows pass): `icon-muted` inline SVG glyphs (`RowGlyph.vue`) replace the date on the focused or hovered row only. Accessible names, roving tab stops and the `meta-compact` disclosure stay. The disclosure now also re-measures on text-size changes inside an unchanged row box (rail/contact pass: the sender label is observed too). Remaining: Superhuman shows done/snooze/more; we show only our real actions (read/unread, done).
214	8. **Date-group caption.** Done (rows pass): title case, 12px `text-secondary`, a 48px block, no rule, on the content inset. A leading Today caption is visually hidden (gap 3).
215	9. **Contact pane.** Done (2026-11-07 rail/contact layout pass; type from the typeset pass). A fixed 272px column on Deep Umber with a `0 24px 24px` inset.
216	   - **No visible caption:** the "Focused conversation" / "Open conversation" h2 stays in the accessibility tree (visually hidden).
217	   - **Pinned lines:** the name (16px regular Headline) is centered on the tab line at 42px and wraps around that center before it moves anything. The email (12px semibold Title) is centered on the first list line at 96px.
218	   - **Copy controls:** each copy control is a 16px Graphite glyph in the trailing slot of its own line, revealed by opacity on line hover or focus. It stays focusable, and it no longer leaves an empty line when hidden. Without a display name, Copy email moves to the name line.
219	   - **Recent cached mail:** a Title label with a 16px envelope glyph (~129px), then plain Ash text rows at a 24px pitch (first at 156px). Each row has an ellipsis and the full subject as its title, rises to Paper White on hover or focus, and is still a button.
220	   - **Narrow disclosure:** inside the Contact disclosure below 1000px, the same content stacks compactly under the drawer header.
221	   - **No footer toolbar:** Account, Activity and Drafts stay in the rail, their one home. The contact column does not exist below 1000px and is `inert` while a drawer is open, so footer toggles would vanish on narrow viewports and could not close their own drawer or receive focus back.
222	   Remaining: the label keeps our honest copy "Recent cached mail" rather than "Mail" (vocabulary pass). The list is still the 4 most recent cached results from the sender search, not a provider-complete thread list.
223	10. **Palette deltas.** Done: `text-primary` #ece9e2 → #ffffff (typeset pass), `text-secondary` #a8a29a → #c0bcb6 (rows pass), `text-tertiary`, `icon-muted` and `unread-marker` added (header and rows passes), the undefined `--text-muted` on coverage notes now maps to `text-secondary`, and `rail-well` / `rail-button` are CSS tokens (rail pass). `divider` is now #474543 (polish pass): the rail and contact-pane seams, the drawer's leading edge, utility-chip and input borders, the compact row-actions popover and the command-overlay hint rule. It never separates rows (the list has no row borders). The old #3b3936 survives as the quieter `rule` token for structure inside a pane, only in the reader (toolbar and message rules) and inside drawers (Activity and draft rows, group detail, Account panel, Reminders fieldset), so those surfaces keep their tone until a reader reference is captured. `focus-accent` stays at the committed #bba5ed; the capture reads about #bfa1f6, which is within capture and color-profile noise.
224	11. **Global button style.** Done (polish pass). The `button` defaults are zero-specificity (`:where()`), so every component class keeps its own look. The default is a ghost: transparent, Paper White, 4px radius, `4px 8px` (24px tall at 12px, the old chip's hit target), Lifted Charcoal on hover, Focus Stone on press, 0.45 opacity when disabled, and the 2px Dusk Lavender focus ring at a 1px offset. The selection bar, the action notice's Undo, Load more, the search form and the reader toolbar are ghost text buttons. Bordered `button-utility` chips (Lifted Charcoal, 1px Seam, `3px 8px`) appear only inside utility drawers, the modal attachment chooser, recovery banners (`.recovery-banner`: draft-close recovery, inbox/account load errors, the reader's navigation error, the header's saved-split error) and the synthetic workspace strip. Fields follow "Inputs / Fields": a Seam border that shifts to Dusk Lavender (plus a 1px inner outline) on keyboard focus, Smoke placeholders (4.76:1 on Lifted Charcoal) and a lavender ring on native checkboxes.
225	12. **Command overlay.** Done (polish pass; structure pass: groups, per-command glyphs, aliases, Keys list, "no match" copy, caption removed). The off-palette values the overlay still carried (#56534e border and rules, #c9c4bc caption, icon and hint text, #d4cfc7 disabled reasons, #66615b `kbd` fill, `.85rem` radius, the 46rem width, 24px query and 1.5rem glyph) are now tokens: a 576px Lifted Charcoal panel with a 10px radius, no border, Overlay lift over a `rgba(0,0,0,0.53)` backdrop at 15vh. The query is 16px on Deep Umber with a 1px Dusk Lavender border, items are 36px rows of 12px Body with 16px Graphite glyphs, the highlighted item is Focus Stone plus a 3px Dusk Lavender bar, disabled items are Smoke with Ash reasons, and `kbd` is Ash on Deep Umber. Geometry is whole-pixel so a highlighted item scrolled into view is never clipped. The modal attachment chooser shares the panel (46rem wide, 12px body), which closes the "chooser body inherits 16px" remainder of gap 14. (The violets this gap once listed were already gone before this pass.)
226	13. **In-flow bars.** Done (polish pass). Every bar is borderless Body type with its text on the 50px content inset and 6px block padding. The lines that come and go with triage keys (the Selection bar, the single-slot Action notice and the command-error alert) now live in a bottom dock of the list column (`.list-dock`) instead of above the list, so x, e and z never move a row. Measured at 1280×800 (Gmail preview): the first row stays at y=126 (real clock) or y=78 (Today clock) through x, x, Clear, e and z; before, it moved 126 → 186.9 → 162.8 → 156. 232	## 2. Colors
233	
234	One warm charcoal ramp, one violet signal, and two status hues reserved for truth-telling.
235	
236	### Primary
237	- **Dusk Lavender** (`focus-accent`): the single "you are here" signal. Used for the 4px bar on the focused row, the active message bar in the reader, focus outlines, and the highlighted command. It never fills an area and never decorates.
238	
239	### Secondary
240	- **Orchid Dot** (`unread-marker`): only for the 5px unread dot in the row gutter. It is pinker than Dusk Lavender so that unread and focus never read as the same signal.
241	
242	### Neutral
243	- **Warm Charcoal** (`surface`): the list, rail and header plane. Everything sits on it.
244	- **Deep Umber** (`surface-contact`): the contact pane and utility drawers. It is one step darker, so context reads as secondary to the list.
245	- **Lifted Charcoal** (`surface-raised`): utility chips, overlays and inputs.
246	- **Focus Stone** (`focus-fill`): the focused-row and active-message fill, and the highlighted command item.
247	- **Inkwell** (`rail-well`): the pill behind the rail's navigation glyphs.
248	- **Rail Pebble** (`rail-button`): the circular rail action button.
249	- **Paper White** (`text-primary`): sender, subject, active tab, contact name and email, labels.
250	- **Ash** (`text-secondary`): snippet, date, group caption, contact threads, counts.
251	- **Smoke** (`text-tertiary`): inactive split tabs.
252	- **Graphite** (`icon-muted`): every resting glyph (row actions, compose, search, hamburger, footer icons, attachment). Hover and focus raise glyphs to Paper White.
253	- **Seam** (`divider`): the 1px vertical separators between rail, list and contact pane, and the drawer's leading edge; also the 1px border of utility chips, fields and floating panels. Never between rows.
254	- **Rule** (`rule`): a quieter 1px structure line inside a pane, used only in the reader and inside drawers. Never in the list.
255	
256	### Status
257	- **Amber Notice** (`warning`): pending, outcome unknown, local-only, expired-undo and partial states.
258	- **Coral Fault** (`danger`): confirmed failures and command errors.
259	
260	### Named Rules
261	**The One Signal Rule.** Dusk Lavender appears at most once per screen, on the current row or message. If two violet things are visible, one of them is wrong.
262	
263	**The Seams-Only Rule.** Dividers separate panes, never rows. Rows are separated by rhythm alone.
264	
265	**The Status-Is-Sacred Rule.** Amber and coral are never used decoratively, and a status is never shown only as a tint: every status carries words.
266	
267	## 3. Typography
268	
269	**Body Font:** system-ui (with -apple-system, sans-serif)
270	**Label/Mono Font:** ui-monospace, for plain-text message bodies only
271	
272	**Character:** One local system sans in two weights carries the whole UI. Hierarchy comes from weight (600 vs 400) and tone (Paper White vs Ash), not size. The browsing shell uses just two sizes.
273	
274	### Hierarchy
275	- **Headline** (400, 1rem / 16px, 1.25): split tabs and the contact name. This is the only large text in the shell.
276	- **Title** (600, 0.75rem / 12px, 1.35): sender names, contact email, section labels ("Mail"), footer labels, notice labels.
277	- **Body** (400, 0.75rem / 12px, 1.35): subject (Paper White), snippet and threads (Ash), date-group captions (Ash).
278	- **Label** (400, 0.75rem / 12px, tabular numerals): dates ("8:00 AM", "6 NOV" with an uppercase month) and counts in status text.
279	- **Mono** and the other steps are CSS tokens: `--type-headline`, `--type-body`, `--type-count`, `--type-mono`, `--weight-regular`, `--weight-strong` (`src/assets/style.css`). Use the tokens, never a literal size.
280	
281	### Dates
282	Row and reader dates are one fixed product format, not a locale format. They depend only on the instant, the current time and the viewer's time zone (`src/lib/browsing-dates.ts`). Month group captions ("October 2026") still follow the locale.
283	- **Row, today:** the time, 12-hour, no leading zero: "8:00 AM", "12:05 PM".
284	- **Row, earlier this calendar year:** day and month: "6 NOV". The DOM text is "6 Nov"; CSS uppercases it, so screen readers hear a word, not letters.
285	- **Row, any other year (past or future):** day, month and four-digit year: "9 JAN 2025". The day is kept for precision, and a two-digit year would read as another day.
286	- **Unknown or unparsable:** "Unknown" in the row, "Unknown date" in full form. Never blank.
287	- **Full form** (reader message times, the row date's hover title): "Thu 9 Jan 2025, 6:29 PM". The same 12-hour clock as the row.
288	- Every rendered date is a `<time>` with a normalized ISO `datetime` when the timestamp parses.
289	- **Count** (400, 0.6875rem / 11px): split-tab counts, set 4px after the tab label.
290	- **Mono** (400, 0.85rem, 1.45): the current plain-text message body in the reader.
291	
292	Sizes are rem so the 16px and 20px root-font layouts in `tests/inbox-list.rendered-layout.test.ts` still scale. Row and header heights are min-heights in px. The 12px row size is measured from the capture: system-ui glyph metrics point to 11.5–12px.
293	
294	### Named Rules
295	**The Two-Size Rule.** The browsing shell uses 16px and 12px only (11px for counts). A third size in the list needs a written reason.
296	
297	**The No-Caps-Caption Rule.** No uppercase letter-spaced captions in the browsing shell. Date groups and pane headings are title case. Uppercase is allowed only for the month in compact dates.
298	
299	## 4. Elevation
300	
301	The browsing shell is flat. Depth comes from tonal layering: Warm Charcoal for the plane, Deep Umber for context, Focus Stone for the current row, Inkwell for the rail well. No shadows sit on rows, panes, the header or the rail. Shadows appear only on surfaces that truly float above the shell and cover it.
302	
303	### Shadow Vocabulary
304	- **Drawer cast** (`box-shadow: -8px 0 24px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.35)`): the right-edge utility drawer (Activity, Account, Drafts).
305	- **Popover lift** (`box-shadow: 0 6px 16px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.35)`): the compact row-actions disclosure panel.
306	- **Overlay lift** (`box-shadow: 0 16px 64px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.53)`): the command palette and navigator, over a `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.53)` backdrop (`--overlay-lift`, `--overlay-backdrop`).
307	
308	### Named Rules
309	**The Flat-Shell Rule.** If something in the rail, header, list or contact pane casts a shadow, remove it. Shadows mean "this covers the shell", nothing else.
310	
311	## 5. Components
312	
313	### Conversation Row (signature)
314	The core of the product: dense, quiet and exact.
315	- **Shape:** square corners (0), a fixed 36px height, inset 6px from both pane edges.
316	- **Layout:** a 44px gutter (unread dot, or the checkbox in selection mode), then a 132px sender (Title, Paper White, ellipsis), then the subject (Body, Paper White) and snippet (Body, Ash) on one line with 12px gaps, then the trailing date (Label, Ash) about 25px from the pane edge. An attachment glyph (Graphite, 16px) sits before the date, three-state like the read marker: a solid paperclip when attachments are known present, a quieter outline paperclip when the attachment state is unknown, and nothing when known absent. Done (2026-11-07 P3 three-state glyph; the unknown state is named "Attachment state unknown" in the accessible name and title, never rendered as silence).
317	- **Focused:** Focus Stone fill plus a 4px Dusk Lavender bar on the fill's own left edge. The date gives way to three action glyphs (done, snooze, more) at a 32px pitch.
318	- **Hover:** a barely-there lift (`rgba(255,255,255,0.03)`). Action glyphs appear; focus and read state never change.
319	- **Pending / unknown:** an Amber Notice word ("Pending…") in the meta region, never just a tint.
320	- **Selected:** the visible checkbox plus a secondary inset bar, so selection never relies on color alone and never replaces the focus bar.
321	
322	### Date Group Caption
323	- **Style:** Body, Ash, title case ("Yesterday"), on the 50px content inset, in a 48px block. No rule and no background band. Not focusable.
324	- **Leading Today:** visually hidden (kept for assistive technology), so a list that opens with today's mail starts on the first list line. Every other leading caption stays visible.
325	
326	### Split Tabs (Navigation)
327	- **Style:** Headline type. The active tab is Paper White; inactive tabs are Smoke. The count (11px, Ash) follows 4px after the label and disappears at zero. Tabs are spaced 18px apart.
328	- **Header:** 78px tall, no bottom border. The hamburger is a Graphite glyph to the left of the inset; compose and search are Graphite glyphs on the right, at the row-action pitch.
329	
330	### Rail
331	- **Style:** 40px wide on Warm Charcoal, with a 1px Seam on its right. The top action, Inbox, is a 28px Rail Pebble circle centered on the tab line. The other destination glyphs sit in a 30px Inkwell pill at a 28px pitch, with the first glyph on the first list line. Utilities (Account, Activity, Drafts, and Contact below 1000px) are ghost glyphs at the bottom. The active destination glyph is Paper White on a 24px Rail Pebble disc; the rest are Graphite.
332	- **Labels:** icon-only on screen. Every button keeps its text label as its accessible name, a `title`, and a keyboard tooltip on `:focus-visible`.
333	- **Activity badge:** an Amber Notice count of unresolved operations (pending plus outcome unknown), named in words by the button's description and title.
334	
335	### Contact Pane
336	- **Style:** 272px on Deep Umber, with a 1px Seam on its left and a 24px inset. No visible caption heading (it stays for assistive tech).
337	- **Content:** the name in Headline on the tab line; the email in Title on the first list line; copy glyphs in each line's trailing slot, revealed on hover or focus; a section label (Title with a 16px glyph) followed by recent threads (Body, Ash, ellipsis, 24px pitch); exact known data only, never invented enrichment.
338	- **Footer:** none. Superhuman's footer toolbar has no counterpart with real actions here; the utilities live in the rail (Parity gap 9).
339	
340	### Buttons
341	- **Ghost (browsing shell, the default):** transparent, Paper White text or a Graphite glyph, 4px radius, `4px 8px` (24px tall). Text ghosts in the dock bars (selection actions, Undo, Load more) carry the Title weight. Hover lifts a text ghost to Lifted Charcoal and a glyph to Paper White; press is Focus Stone; disabled is 0.45 opacity. The focus ring is a 2px Dusk Lavender outline at a 1px offset.
342	- **Utility (drawers, the attachment chooser, recovery banners):** a Lifted Charcoal fill with a 1px Seam border, 4px radius, `3px 8px` (24px tall); hover is Focus Stone. This is the only bordered button.
343	- **Specificity:** the defaults are `:where()` rules, so a component class (split tab, rail item, row action, contact line) always wins without `!important`.
344	
345	### Command Overlay
346	- **Style:** a Lifted Charcoal panel, 10px radius, 576px max width, no border, Overlay lift, 15vh from the top. There is no caption: the placeholder and the dialog's accessible name say whether it is Commands or Destinations. The 38px query (16px Headline) sits on Deep Umber with a 1px Dusk Lavender border; it always owns keyboard focus, so that border is its focus indicator. Items are 36px rows of 12px Body with a 16px Graphite glyph that turns Paper White when highlighted. The highlighted item gets a Focus Stone fill plus a 3px Dusk Lavender left bar. Disabled items are Smoke, with their reason in Ash. Shortcuts are `kbd` in Ash on Deep Umber, compact ("G then E", timing in the tooltip). The hint line sits under a 1px Seam.
347	- **Groups (palette only):** Conversation, Selection, View, Go to, each a sentence-case 11px Ash label, no rule, no caps. The Destinations navigator is one group and stays unlabelled. Items are searched by label, aliases (undo → revert, archive → done, snooze → remind) and their exact bound key; the empty state says what did not match ("No command matches “…”.").
348	- **Glyphs:** `CommandGlyph.vue` reuses RowGlyph, HeaderGlyph and PaneGlyph where the idea already has a glyph, and draws the few palette-only ones (open, undo, selection, splits, filter, switch account) on the same 16px grid.
349	- **Keys:** a quiet list under the commands for bound keys that are not commands (J/K, X, Shift+J/K, Left). They are text rows, never options: no highlight, no pointer, never executed. Filtered by the same query.
350	
351	### Inputs / Fields
352	- **Style:** a Lifted Charcoal fill, a 1px Seam border, 4px radius, inherited font.
353	- **Focus:** the border shifts to Dusk Lavender, doubled by a 1px inner outline so the ring reads at 12px. No glow.
354	- **Placeholder:** Smoke (4.76:1 on Lifted Charcoal).
355	
356	### In-flow Notices (Action notice, Selection bar, coverage and recovery)
357	- **Style:** borderless lines in normal flow, with text on the 50px content inset, in Body type with 6px block padding. Status words use Amber Notice or Coral Fault. Undo shows its `kbd` hint in Ash. They never overlay rows and never auto-hide a failure.
358	- **Bottom dock (transient lines):** the Selection bar, the Action notice and the command-error alert sit in a dock at the bottom of the list column, below the list, never above it. Showing or hiding them never moves a row. The dock reserves one 36px line and grows upward into the list viewport; the focused row is kept whole when the viewport shrinks. Its lines are whole-pixel (16px line height, 24px buttons). This is the honest, in-flow form of Superhuman's bottom undo toast: no float, no shadow, nothing covered.
359	- **Above the list (static lines):** Starred/Done coverage notes and the draft-close recovery banner, which belong to the destination or to a pending recovery rather than to the last keystroke.
360	
361	## 6. Do's and Don'ts
362	
363	### Do:
364	- **Do** keep rows at exactly 36px with 12px type, and separate them by rhythm alone.
365	- **Do** align split tabs, sender names, date captions, notices and the bottom dock to the single 50px content inset.
366	- **Do** use Dusk Lavender (#bba5ed) only for the current row or message, and the focus ring.
367	- **Do** show every pending, partial, failed and outcome-unknown state in words, in Amber Notice or Coral Fault, where the user is already looking.
368	- **Do** align the contact pane to the list: the name on the tab line, the email on the first-row line.
369	- **Do** ship glyphs as local inline SVG with an accessible name. No icon fonts and no CDN.
370	- **Do** name each action once, in sentence case, on every surface (row glyph, selection bar, reader, Activity, action notice, palette): "Mark done" / "Mark not done" (E / Shift+E), "Mark read" / "Mark unread", "Star" / "Unstar". Counted forms keep the verb: "Mark 3 done". Destinations keep their proper names (Inbox, Done, Starred, Trash, Provider mail, Activity) after "Go to". "Archive" is the provider-side effect, never a label; it survives only as a palette search alias.
371	- **Do** treat Superhuman's browsing look as the visual and interaction reference. Close look parity is the goal (PRODUCT.md).
372	
373	### Don't:
374	- **Don't** draw dividers between rows or under the header. Seams separate panes only.
375	- **Don't** use uppercase letter-spaced captions in the browsing shell.
376	- **Don't** add Gmail-web clutter: toolbars of rarely-used icons, or chrome competing with content.
377	- **Don't** add "AI magic" chrome: sparkle icons, or generated summaries presented as fact.
378	- **Don't** build a Superhuman feature-parity clone. Copy the browsing look, not Superhuman's product scope.
379	- **Don't** use generic SaaS dashboard aesthetics: card grids, gradient heroes, oversized rounded panels, decorative illustration.
380	- **Don't** show optimistic UI that lies: no "Done" toast before the provider confirms, and no silent retry of an ambiguous send.
381	- **Don't** put shadows on anything in the rail, header, list or contact pane.
382	- **Don't** introduce a third type size in the list, or use off-palette hex values (the old command-overlay violets are the cautionary example).
383	- **Don't** load remote fonts, images or CDN assets.

# Development guide

This repository contains two deliberately separate native profiles: the durable
synthetic fixture slice (Slice 01) and an explicit Gmail profile built in stages.
Slice 02 adds system-browser OAuth/PKCE, a macOS Keychain credential store,
bounded inbox caching, and background sync. Slice 03 adds opt-in, durable Gmail
archive/unarchive and explicit read/unread actions; Gmail remains read-only until
the user explicitly requests the broader Google `gmail.modify` permission.
Slice 04 adds a local-only plain-text composer and durable draft recovery, but
still does not send/delete mail or expose arbitrary labels. Opening a message
never marks it read. UX-05 adds bounded multi-select and durable bulk
archive/read group processing with one-level partial group Undo; the browser
preview remains synthetic and in-memory. See
the slice contracts for individual acceptance scope. UX-08 adds narrow Gmail-mode
Star/Unstar singles/groups, durable Undo/reconciliation, cache-only Starred and a
single cached starred filter; see [its contract and validation ledger](ux-08-stars.md).
The legacy native fixture remains archive-only; unsupported star controls are
absent there. No real provider writes are authorized by implementation tests.
UX-06 adds one durable local
sender/domain split over Inbox, exact cached-count badges, and a single unread
filter. See [the saved-split contract](ux-06-saved-split.md) for matching,
keyboard navigation, cache coverage, and persistence boundaries.

## Layout

| Path | Owner |
|---|---|
| `crates/mail-core/` | Rust DTOs, fixture core, Gmail provider/auth/cache/sync/actions, SQLite, profile locks |
| `src/`, `tests/`, `package.json`, configs | Vue 3/TypeScript frontend, IPC adapter and tests |
| `src/lib/ipc/generated.ts` | **Generated** — do not edit by hand; regenerate with `mise run gen:ts` |
| `src-tauri/` | Thin Tauri 2 shell: typed mail/draft/close commands, `mailbox_changed` and `drafts_changed` hints, fixture/Gmail profile selection and lifecycle |
| `mise.toml` | Project tasks (see below) |

## UX-09 increment A: read-only provider mail

The **Provider mail** rail entry (Gmail native or labelled browser preview) opens
a bounded destination browser for Sent, provider Drafts, All Mail, Spam, Trash
and user labels. Search covers the loaded catalog; Show more expands it. It is
not mailbox search. All Mail excludes Spam/Trash. Every page contains at most
25 conversations, at most 16 MiB of serialized thread DTOs, and no exact total.
The read-only drawer intentionally has no triage/reply controls. Its page remains
mounted during a reader visit; closing the drawer returns to the prior inbox
context. This is not yet the roadmap's integrated main-list destination context.

Native commands `list_provider_destinations(accountId, cached)` and
`browse_provider_destination(request)` run off the UI thread, require the active
account, and use readonly Gmail APIs. Page cursors carry account+destination
identity and a bounded opaque provider token; they grant no authority.
A separate SQLite table retains one catalog and up to 20 destination snapshots
(latest successful page per retained destination), independent of inbox discovery,
history and operation recovery. **Use saved catalog/page** is explicit and
timestamped; provider failures are never silently converted to saved success or
an empty list. Restart retains these snapshots; disconnect clears them.

Provider Drafts are read-only snapshots, **not** the app's local editable drafts.
The native fixture rejects both provider commands; browser preview models them
in memory only. Label/Move, label badges on ordinary inbox rows, palette integration,
and saved-view/search criteria are not implemented here. After rebasing onto
`b4972ee`, the UX-06/07/08 contracts are preserved but not extended by this
increment. See [the increment contract](ux-09-provider-destinations.md)
for evidence and remaining gates.

# UX-12 — bounded download-only attachments

## Contract (implementation scope)

Base inspected: `6c30b9c` (UX-05); UX-06/07 are absent and not prerequisites.
No cross-thread changes. Existing reader visits, account-scoped cache, local
drafts, close protocol, setters, bulk receipts and Undo remain unchanged.

Journey: reader → Files and links / native Cmd+O → choose a known cached file
or literal HTTP(S) body link → explicitly save / confirm external browser →
dismiss to exact reader expansion, scroll and focus. Email addresses remain
participant/draft exits, never `mailto:` links. No automatic opening.

Rust owns descriptors, authenticated readonly Gmail fetch and file validation.
Descriptors are cached transactionally in SQLite alongside sync facts; legacy
cache has no descriptors until sync. Bounded to 32 descriptors/thread, nesting
16, request/message IDs 256 bytes, opaque attachment handles 4096 bytes,
filename 160 characters, 5 MiB/file. Both ID classes must be nonempty and contain
only ASCII letters, digits, `-` or `_`; no path/query/fragment delimiters,
percent escapes, padding, controls or non-ASCII. The attachment-specific 4 KiB
ceiling accommodates production-shaped handles longer than 256 bytes (including
the reported 404-character example), with headroom while still bounding GET path
length and cached metadata (at most 32 handles/thread). This is a local defensive
limit, not a claim about Gmail's maximum handle length. Discovery and authenticated
attachment GET use the same attachment validator; request/message validation and
provider URL/authority construction are unchanged. Oversized,
unknown-size and missing attachment bodies fail closed. Fetch verifies cached
account+conversation+message+attachment identity, generation and cancellation.
Retained snapshots cannot fetch; no new scope or mutation permission.

Save is deliberately narrow: a new uniquely named file in the OS Downloads
folder, never a frontend path and never overwrite. Sender filenames are reduced
to ASCII inert names; every download ends `.download` (including Office/HTML),
with no file execution/reveal/automatic external document handler. User can
inspect/rename a saved file outside the app. Saved files are user-owned exports
and remain in Downloads after disconnect; cache cleanup does not delete them.
Acknowledgement follows sync_all;
failed/cancelled partial files are removed (a crash can leave an inert partial
file; there is no resumable-download promise). A blocked HTTP call can take its
existing 30-second timeout to return; cancellation is checked before/after calls,
while reading chunks, and before local publication. Cancellation uses the
existing typed `auth_cancelled` error, not an OAuth state transition.
No durable remote intent is needed:
this is a readonly transfer, not a mailbox operation. Lost save ACK can leave a
completed unique download; retry may create another and is not exactly-once.

Only syntactically valid MIME descriptors are admitted; PDF signatures must
match PDF declarations; text/plain must be UTF-8 without NUL, and obvious HTML
document prefixes are rejected. Unsupported MIME is saved inert, never rendered. Signature/length/base64 checks reject
observable corruption; this is not structural PDF/Office validation or a malware
scanner. No raw bytes/base64/credentials reach Vue.
External links allow only bounded HTTP(S), host required, no credentials or
controls; Rust revalidates before system browser dispatch on macOS. Other OS
external dispatch is unavailable, not a simulated success.

# Critique run 1: reader + reply/compose

Method: single-agent, code-and-test verification only. Nothing was rendered (no Chrome on this VM, no screenshots), so every visual claim below is read from CSS and templates, not measured. The prior whole-app review scored this area 22/40 and ranked it next (attention 8/10). Each of its findings was re-checked against the code and tests; verdicts are marked CONFIRMED, PARTLY WRONG or REJECTED. Inbox list and search were critiqued earlier and are out of scope.

## Heuristics 23/40
| # | Heuristic | Score | Key issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Visibility of system status | 3 | "Saved locally / Saving locally…" exists but sits beside a 3-line disclaimer and is amber at rest |
| 2 | Match system / real world | 2 | Raw `conversationId · messageId` in the composer; "N bytes"; "Prepare reply" |
| 3 | User control and freedom | 3 | Esc flushes and closes, Discard confirms; no keyboard way to start a reply |
| 4 | Consistency and standards | 2 | Two reply glyphs; quoted block in mono while the body is proportional; reply form unlike every other reply UI |
| 5 | Error prevention | 3 | Fields disabled while a reply is unprepared; conflict and recovery paths are solid |
| 6 | Recognition rather than recall | 2 | No reply entry in the palette or key hints; the shortcut list says nothing about reply |
| 7 | Flexibility and efficiency | 2 | Reading is fully keyboard-driven (J/K/N/P/O/E/S/Z); replying is mouse-only |
| 8 | Aesthetic and minimalist design | 1 | Up to six caveat paragraphs above the thread; a 4-field form plus 3-line note plus ID line above 3 lines of typing room |
| 9 | Error recovery | 3 | Retry save, Save as new, Reload saved are explicit and honest |
| 10 | Help and documentation | 2 | A permanent disclaimer is doing the job a status line and a title should do |
| | **Total** | **23/40** | Acceptable |

Why 23 and not 22: `useDrafts.statusLabel` already yields an honest settled state ("Saved locally"), so the fix for the disclaimer is to promote that line, not invent a new one.

## Findings: verification

### 1. No reply shortcut — CONFIRMED, P1
`grep` finds no `r` binding anywhere in `App.vue`'s `onKeydown`, and `browsing-actions.ts` has no `reply` action. `prepareReply` (App.vue:1587) is reached only from `ReaderView` emitting `prepareReply`, from two controls: the header glyph `data-test="prepare-reply"` (ReaderView:710-720) and a per-message glyph on the active latest message (ReaderView:848-862). Reading is fully keyboard-driven (J/K/N/P/O/E/S/Z/C); replying is the one step that needs the pointer, which breaks "keyboard first" in the middle of the triage loop.
Safety already holds for a new key: the dispatcher returns for editable targets and IME (`isComposing`/`keyCode 229`, App.vue:1867-1869), returns early while a composer owns keys (App.vue:1866), and `actionShortcutBlocked` lets message toggles through but blocks other buttons. Reply must stay reader-only: the list holds no loaded message, so a list-level R would have to open, load and then reply, which is new scope. The source stays the displayed latest message (never the focused one), and the key must be unavailable for Cached Trash (`browsingOnly`), blocked replies (retained snapshot, incomplete, header mismatch), non-ready state and an open drawer.
Fix: add `reply` to `browsingActions` (label unchanged: "Prepare reply", shortcut R, so existing accessible names stay), `actionGroupOf`, `actionAliases` (respond, answer, write back), `actionAvailable`, `executeAction`, and the key handler; surface "R" in the header glyph title and palette; drive the reader's button titles from `actionLabel('reply')`.

### 2. Reply composer is a form — CONFIRMED, P1
`DraftEditorCore` renders four always-visible labelled fields (To, Cc, Subject, Body) in a 2-column grid (`.composer-fields`, style.css:1819), with a body that is `min-height: 8rem` (5rem when docked, style.css:2070). The core already pre-fills To and `Re: …` Subject for a reply (asserted in `reply-composer.component.test.ts:88-90`), so showing them as empty-looking boxes asks the user to re-read fields they never need to touch. Cc is optional and never filled for a reply. The new-message card needs To and Subject visible (they start empty) but Cc is rarely used.
Fix: reply surface gets a one-line recipient row ("To  Ada Fixture"), Cc and Subject behind a quiet "Cc / Subject" disclosure, and the body is the dominant, auto-focused field. New message keeps To and Subject visible and puts Cc on demand. The To row must never misrepresent the field: show the display name only while To is still the default sender mailbox, and the raw text once edited. Existing `data-test` hooks stay on the inputs; tests that read Cc or Subject reveal them first.
Quoted source: `.reply-quoted` is `--font-mono` at `--type-mono` (0.85rem), larger than the 12px shell and the proportional reading face above it (style.css, ReplyComposer.vue:154-165). Switch to the UI face at the body size in `--text-secondary` (4.99:1 on Focus Stone, ≥ 7:1 on `surface-raised`), keep the 2px rule and pre-wrap, keep it read-only and out of `bodyText`.

### 3. Permanent disclaimer and raw IDs — CONFIRMED, P1
`DraftEditorCore.vue:90-93` prints three lines on every open, every surface: "Local-only plain text. No Send action exists. Recipient text is stored raw… Cc is optional; Bcc, reply-all, quoted text, and rich text are not supported." It also contradicts the UI: it says quoted text is unsupported directly above a quoted block. `ReplyComposer.vue:110-112` and `DraftsPanel.vue:148` print `Reply source is fixed: <conversationId> · <messageId>`: opaque provider IDs a person cannot act on. The settled status line is `.draft-status`, which is colored `--warning` even when everything is fine, so amber at rest dilutes "local-only" as a real warning.
Fix: one line, "Saved locally · not sent" (settled, Ash) / "Saving locally…" / "Save not confirmed" (Amber Notice), with the detail ("Local plain-text draft. Nothing is sent. Recipients are stored as typed and not validated. Bcc, reply-all and rich text are not supported.") in the `title` and a visually hidden description for assistive tech. Drop the ID line from every surface; keep the IDs only as `data-source-*` attributes that tests can read (no visible text). The drawer's own `draft-local-note` in `DraftsPanel` stays (a different surface), but the editor core no longer duplicates it.
Footer: today it is `Close editor` / `Discard…` as equal ghosts with no key hint. Close already flushes (saves) first, and Esc does the same. Fix: primary "Save and close" (Esc kbd hint, Focus Stone fill, Title weight), secondary "Discard…" as an Ash ghost. Honesty is unchanged: the button still waits on the flush and the editor stays open with the error if it fails. No Send, ever.

### 4. Reader header caveats — CONFIRMED, P1
ReaderView:778-816 stacks up to six paragraphs under the subject before the first message: star line, reply-blocked, retained snapshot, one of three read-only/no-auto-read variants, unsupported-or-incomplete, pending. Two are standing statements repeated on every open: "Opening this conversation does not change read state; use an explicit read control" (Gmail with actions) and "Read-only Gmail view: messages are never marked as read. Opening this conversation does not change read state." (Gmail read-only), plus the Cached Trash text. The rest are real exceptions and should stay.
Fix: one muted status line in the existing meta row ("Unread" / "Read-only · Unread"), with the full sentence in its `title` and as visually hidden text, so the guarantee stays discoverable without repeating on screen. Keep every exception inline and amber: reply blocked, retained snapshot, unsupported/incomplete, pending, star attention. Keep the `reader-readonly` / `reader-no-auto-read` hooks on the status line. The Trash notice drops its "Opening does not change read state." sentence and keeps what Trash actually restricts.

### 5. Quoted blocks and signatures force monospace — CONFIRMED, P2
`bodyNeedsMonospace` returns true on the first line matching `^ {0,3}>`, so every reply-chain message renders entirely in mono (message-body-format.ts); two consecutive 4-space-indented lines (signatures, lists) do the same. The quoted tail is also what makes most real threads long.
Fix: split a plain-text body deterministically into prose, an optional signature (after a `-- ` delimiter, only when the tail is short) and an optional trailing quote (an "On … wrote:" attribution line, or a contiguous run of `>` lines to the end). Decide monospace from the prose part only, render signature and quote in the reading face in Ash, and put the quote behind a "Show quoted text" disclosure (per message, kept in the visit state so it survives J/K round trips). Still literal text via interpolation, the `>` characters are never rewritten, nothing is dropped, and interleaved (inline) quotes stay in place and keep the mono rule. The collapsed-row snippet uses the prose part so a message that is mostly quote does not preview as `>`.

### 6. Attachments are second-class — CONFIRMED, P2
`ReaderView` never references `Message.hasAttachment` (a known-true/false/unknown DTO field). Attachments are reachable only through the Cmd+O chooser (a modal). `AttachmentChooser.vue:91` prints `{{ file.size }} bytes` (a 4,812,333-byte file reads as a 7-digit number), and a 230-character paragraph sits above the list (lines 84-85). Its two lists share the same flat style.
Fix: inline attachment rows under the expanded body of each message that has files: name, human size ("27 B", "4.6 MB"), a Save button, and a Cancel while transferring, with the same pending/status/error semantics as the chooser (extract the save/cancel state into one shared composable, no second implementation). Where `hasAttachment === true` but no descriptor is cached, say so plainly ("Attachment not available offline: sync to fetch"); where it is unknown, show nothing (never inferred). Over-5-MiB files say "Over 5 MiB limit". The chooser keeps its role for links and the full list, loses the raw byte counts, and its intro paragraph shrinks to one line with the rest in a `title`/muted note ("Download only. Files save inert with a .download suffix.").

### 7. Loading state and type system — PARTLY WRONG
- Loading: the bare "Loading conversation…" shows only when the shell has no row identity (`loadingIdentity` null: Activity/Reminders/recent-mail entry). From the list the reader already shows the row's subject, sender and date first (ReaderView:735-742, tested). The holding state during J/K keeps the previous conversation on screen. Low value, P3. Small fix only: give the bare line `role="status"`; keep the exact text the smooth-navigation test pins.
- Collapsed sender column — REJECTED. `flex: 0 0 11em` at 12px is 132px, exactly the list's sender column. Its Ash/regular weight is deliberate: only the active message is Paper White/strong, which keeps the One Signal rule. Making it strong would erase that distinction.
- Uppercased date — REJECTED. `.message-time` uppercases the month exactly as `.row-time` does (style.css:1151 vs 1526), and DESIGN.md "Dates" specifies this ("6 Nov" in the DOM, "6 NOV" on screen). The reader already matches the list.
- Reply composer height — CONFIRMED. `.reply-composer { max-height: 45% }` with a 5rem textarea and a 4-field header, a 3-line note and an ID line leaves roughly three lines to type in, and the whole composer scrolls internally. The compact layout in findings 2 and 3 fixes this: the body gets a `min-height` of at least 6 lines and grows, the shell scrolls only when the thread and composer genuinely do not fit.

Graphite `#8e8a87` is 3.0:1 on Warm Charcoal but below 3:1 on Focus Stone `#474644` (about 2.4:1).
